items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And Thelma Hopkins, who used to be in Bosom Buddies

ctx.x: “Tom, where’d you get that suit? I got to get one just like it” – so he comes up to me, and he’s speaking with this accent. After the scene, I said, “You sound just like Dracula.” He wanted my autograph. He was reticent to talk to me. The band started to vamp Killer Joe. I said, “I got to play now, but when I finish, I’ll give you the autograph.” That was the last scene. Then when I gave him the autograph – Steven had gotten me to sign my autograph on a piece of paper, and he used that. I was supposed to sign…

Steven is a down-to-earth guy. He looks you right in the eye. None of that stuff. And Tom. Humble. If you didn’t know who they were, you’d just think it was another guy. Incredible. I love him, and what he does. Tom Hanks has come a long ways. And Thelma Hopkins, who used to be in Bosom Buddies, where he got his start – Thelma Hopkins and him. The two guys played – masqueraded as women.
